title: Per-layer quantized-kernel speculator and prefill scheduler to reduce v3 regression surface
creator: Priya Rao
description: Problem: After initial v3 kernel onboarding, we observed intermittent latency regressions and small quality deltas for certain mixed-precision workloads when v3 kernels are selected aggressively at startup. Goal: Implement a per-layer kernel speculator that chooses between quantized v2 kernels, v3 kernels, and hybrid fallbacks at runtime, combined with a prefill-aware scheduler that staggers v3 activation (a 'hinge' warmup). This should reduce regression surface during traffic spikes while preserving throughput gains for long-context, high-batch workloads.
acceptance_criteria: No P95 latency regression >5% on representative prod-shaped workload during 1-hour rolling canary compared to baseline (runtime-1.21).
End-to-end token-cost delta <= 2% for regulated throughputs when speculator enabled relative to baseline optimized config.
Automatic rollback trigger when quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like evals or endpoint prompt tests) deviate >1.5% for seeded evals.
Unit and integration tests covering kernel selection logic and prefill hinge scheduling with synthetic load harness.
Docs for ops: how to tune hinge slope, per-layer thresholds, and emergency rollbacks are published in Confluence.
design_decisions: Speculator runs a lightweight per-request scorer that uses recent per-layer latency + kv-cache hit rate to pick kernel variant; avoids heavy profiling paths at request time.
Hinge warmup: v3 activation is staged by request-count percentile per node (fast ramp for long-lived sessions, slow ramp for bursty short requests).
Quantized kernels (v2-quant) remain default for short-context low-batch requests to keep tail latency bounded.
Tradeoff: Slightly higher code complexity and new telemetry metrics in exchange for safer rollouts and fewer regressions.
We intentionally avoid global static heuristics; the speculator adapts per-worker with periodic weight sync to control oscillation.

testing_plan: Local: run runtimelib/bench/speculator_bench with FA2/FA3 artifacts and compare kernel choice histogram across shapes.
CI: GPU CI matrix for CUDA 12.1 and 12.3 to catch kernel abi regressions; add stress test that toggles kv-cache hit/miss patterns.
Staging: deterministic replay of production trace for 24h with speculator ON/OFF, compare latency and quality slices.
Canary: 5% production traffic for 1h, with automatic rollback if P95 latency or eval-quality thresholds breached. Observe for oscillation for 6h.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Oscillation between kernels under bursty traffic — Mitigation: add damping via exponential moving average on scorer inputs and require minimum activation duration (30s) per worker.

Risk: Unexpected memory layout differences between v2-quant and v3 kernels leading to OOMs — Mitigation: static workspace budget check during selection and fall back to v2 if memory requirement exceeds threshold.
Risk: Regression unnoticed by token-level metrics — Mitigation: seed prompt evals and per-customer smoke tests run during canary; alerting integrated with pager for deviations.
Risk: Increased cpu overhead for selection logic — Mitigation: keep scorer implementation in native code path with small constant work and offload heavier profiling to background sampler.
canary_plan: Stage 1: Dry run on internal load generator for 2 hours; verify telemetry keys and rollback hooks work.
Stage 2: 5% production traffic to subset of nodes (tag: speculator-canary-1) for 1 hour; monitor latency and quality metrics.
Stage 3: If stable, expand to 20% for 6 hours with longer observation for oscillation; then full rollout behind gradual percentage gate.
Rollback criteria: P95 latency >5% over baseline for 5m sustained OR quality eval delta >1.5% for seeded prompts.
